newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Kinnock to seek backing for Swiss talks stand.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock to seek backing for Swiss talks stand.

text.p: The European Commission will seek a tough-talking statement from EU transport ministers on Friday in an attempt to bolster its efforts to force a deal in EU/Swiss talks on land and air transport relations.

European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock will ask a two-day informal ministerial session in Amsterdam to back his stand on Switzerland's latest offer on lorry transit charges for its territory, which last week he described as "prohibitive".

"We would hope that the ministers would let us know that they are happy with the work we are doing and would give us fairly tough backing for that position," a Commission official told Reuters on Thursday.

One of the main issues, according to the official, includes what price EU operators should pay for driving their 40-tonne trucks across Swiss territory once Berne lifts its existing ban on all trucks exceeding 28-tonnes.

Switzerland's lead negotiator Max Friedli told a news conference after talks last week that Berne had offered a 600-Swiss-franc ($420) charge as the "basis for discussion", comprising a 200 franc transit charge plus a three- centime-per-tonne-kilometre charge per lorry.
The road-pricing system would replace the existing 28-tonner ban, which would be phased-out in stages by 2005.

Ministers will also discuss operational details for Switzerland's planned rail-freight alternative for transit traffic, a safeguard clause offering both sides guarantees in any deal and the question of immediate, mutual access for both sides' trucks to one another's road haulage markets.
The official said the Commission put at between 1.0 and 1.5 million the number of trucks diverted to French and Austrian trans-alpine routes because of Swiss truck-weight limits.
Another item linked to discussions will be Swiss demands for full access to the EU's civil aviation market, which from April 1 will be fully liberalised for licensed operators.

"I doubt that Friday will be the time that these kinds of decisions will be finalised. It's really a progress report, it's neither the time nor the place for a great breakthrough," the official added. ($=1.43 francs)
